rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose Cantonese equivalent for reaching an endpoint in time.

example.english: I’ll stay till ten tonight before I leave.
example.traditional: 我會留到夜晚十點先走。
example.jyutping: ngo5 wui5 lau4 dou3 je6 maan5 sap6 dim2 sin1 zau2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken pattern when B happens only after A, as in 「試過先知」.

example.english: You won't know whether it's tasty till you try it.
example.traditional: 到你試過先知好唔好食。
example.jyutping: dou3 nei5 si3 gwo3 sin1 zi1 hou2 m4 hou2 sik6

rows.note: Use this when an action continues up to a particular time or event.

example.english: I work till evening before I finish for the day.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zou6 dou3 je6 maan5 sin1 sau1 gung1

rows.note: Use this when the sentence specifically involves waiting or postponing B until A.

example.english: We'll wait till the rain stops before going out.
example.traditional: 我哋等到落完雨先出街。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 dang2 dou3 lok6 jyun4 jyu5 sin1 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese term for the cash register itself.

example.english: The till is broken, so get someone to come fix it.
example.traditional: 收銀機壞咗，叫人嚟整吓。
example.jyutping: sau1 ngan4 gei1 waai6 zo2 giu3 jan4 lei4 zing2 haa5

rows.jyutping: sau1 ngan4 gei1 go3 gwai6 tung2
rows.note: Use this specifically for the removable drawer inside the register, not the whole machine.

example.english: I took out the till drawer to count the money.
example.traditional: 我攞出收銀機個櫃桶嚟數錢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 lo2 ceot1 sau1 ngan4 gei1 go3 gwai6 tung2 lei4 sou2 cin2

rows.note: Use this construction for clock times such as “twenty till two.”

example.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 caa1 ng5 fan1 zung1 loeng5 dim2 laa3

rows.note: Use this when “till” means before a specified time or event rather than giving a clock countdown.

example.english: You need to submit the form before the deadline; don’t wait till the last day.
example.traditional: 你要喺截止日期之前交份表，唔好等最後一日。
example.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 hai2 zit3 zi2 jat6 kei4 zi1 cin4 gaau1 fan6 biu2 m4 hou2 dang2 zeoi3 hau6 jat1 jat6

rows.jyutping: sau1 ngan4 gei1 jap6 min6 ge3 cin2
rows.note: Use this when till means the money or contents kept in the register.

example.english: We need to count the money in the till before closing.
example.traditional: 收舖前要點清收銀機入面嘅錢。
example.jyutping: sau1 pou3 cin4 jiu3 dim2 cing1 sau1 ngan4 gei1 jap6 min6 ge3 cin2

rows.note: Use this specifically for a bank teller's cash drawer rather than a shop register.

example.english: The bank clerk opened the till.
example.traditional: 銀行職員打開櫃員錢箱。
example.jyutping: ngan4 hong4 zik1 jyun4 daa2 hoi1 gwai6 jyun4 cin2 soeng1
